title: Helper verbs and the potential
summary: The potential helper る / られる attaches to the え-stem, makes an ichidan verb, and brings the same "thing is possible" logic you saw with 好き.

blocks.text: Remember: Japanese has no conjugation, only **helper words** that plug into stems. The **potential** ("can do") is one of them. It attaches to the **え-stem** and says that the action is **possible**.

For **godan** verbs the helper is just the single kana **る**, added to the え-stem. For **ichidan** verbs it is **られる**. Either way the result is an **ichidan verb**, so it changes like one: 歩ける, 歩けない, 歩けた, 歩けなかった. The potential of する is the separate verb **できる**.

The potential says that something **is possible**, so the thing that is possible is the main carriage and takes **が**. 本が読める is literally "the book is readable". With a hidden carriage, the zero is again the speaker: 読める means "(I) can read".

blocks.en: (I) can read the book. (The book is readable.)

items: Godan: **え-stem + る** (買う → 買える). Ichidan: **drop る + られる**.
来る → **来られる**; する → **できる**.
The result is an **ichidan verb**: 歩ける, 歩けない, 歩けた, 歩けなかった.
The thing that is possible takes **が**: **本が読める**.
